_comment: Tests that only mean something on a real PostgreSQL server with independent connections. CI fails unless every one of them EXECUTED AND PASSED (scripts/assert-required-tests.mjs). Renaming or removing one means updating this list on purpose.
required: concurrency on standard PostgreSQL uses independent database connections
concurrency on standard PostgreSQL parallel mastery confirmations unlock exactly one level
concurrency on standard PostgreSQL parallel confirmations with the SAME key all return one stored result
concurrency on standard PostgreSQL parallel attempt reports with the same key write one row
concurrency on standard PostgreSQL parallel onboarding completions create one puppy and one plan, and generate once
concurrency on standard PostgreSQL parallel first drafts from one owner create one puppy
email rate limits are stored in PostgreSQL is atomic: of 20 simultaneous requests on separate connections exactly 3 pass
daily request limit per account is atomic under concurrency: 25 simultaneous requests are granted exactly 3 units
daily request limit per account the provider call budget is atomic too
reclaiming race: of 10 simultaneous retries of an expired job exactly one takes it over
reclaiming race: of 10 simultaneous new requests over an expired job, one job is started and the old unit is refunded once
the account unit is refunded at most once is atomic: 12 simultaneous refund attempts of one job lower the counter by exactly one
the account unit is refunded at most once is atomic when owners race: a reclaim closing a job and the job closing itself refund once
media concurrency on standard PostgreSQL parallel ingests of different bundles get distinct version numbers
media concurrency on standard PostgreSQL parallel publishes of two versions leave exactly one PUBLISHED version
media lifecycle on standard PostgreSQL parallel publishes of the same reviewed version succeed exactly once
media lifecycle on standard PostgreSQL parallel publishes of two reviewed versions serialise: both succeed in turn and exactly one stays published
media lifecycle on standard PostgreSQL a SAFETY withdrawal racing the publication of the same version leaves it withdrawn and the technique suspended once
media lifecycle on standard PostgreSQL an explicit suspension racing a publication never lets the publication land after the suspension
media lifecycle on standard PostgreSQL parallel suspensions of one technique create one suspension and one event
media generation on standard PostgreSQL a generation commit waits for an in-flight withdrawal and then refuses the withdrawn clip
media generation on standard PostgreSQL a generation commit waits for an in-flight suspension and then refuses the suspended technique
media generation on standard PostgreSQL a withdrawal waits for a generation commit that holds the technique row, so the committed binding predates it
media generation on standard PostgreSQL a withdrawal racing a generation leaves a refused candidate, a binding that predates it, or a free-form plan
media generation on standard PostgreSQL a generation that starts after the withdrawal committed saves a free-form plan with no binding
suspension guard on standard PostgreSQL an attempt waits for an in-flight suspension and is then refused
suspension guard on standard PostgreSQL a mastery confirmation waits for an in-flight suspension and is then refused
suspension guard on standard PostgreSQL a suspension racing mastery confirmations either lets one land first or refuses them, never deadlocks
account deletion on standard PostgreSQL a deletion waits for a generation commit that holds the job row, then removes the committed plan too
account deletion on standard PostgreSQL a generation and an adaptation whose commit starts after the deletion stop at the fence: no row, no refund, never a 500
account deletion on standard PostgreSQL a deletion queued behind the plan lock holds no puppy lock, so progression and deletion never deadlock (both orders)
account deletion on standard PostgreSQL onboarding racing the deletion never leaves a puppy for the deleted user
account deletion on standard PostgreSQL two concurrent deletions of the same account: one succeeds, the other answers UNAUTHENTICATED, no deadlock
account deletion on standard PostgreSQL a job created after the first lock pass cannot deadlock the deletion: the NOWAIT re-lock rolls back and the retry succeeds
allowedToSkip: live model creates, adapts and revises a plan through the real provider
